sentences: [0] Many learners treat errors during practice as signs that they are not yet ready to perform.
[1] They slow down, choose only easy tasks, and feel relieved when nothing goes wrong.
[2] Yet a practice session without mistakes usually teaches very little.
[3] In fact, errors made while practicing are among the most useful information a learner can get.
[4] Each mistake shows exactly where current skill ends, so attention can be directed to that point instead of being spread over what is already known.
[5] Researchers who study musicians, for example, find that the best performers spend most of their practice time on the passages they still play poorly.
[6] In other words, a mistake in practice is not a failure but a map of what to learn next.
stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: (0) 연습 중의 실수는 다음에 배울 지점을 알려 주는 유용한 정보이다.
(1) 실수를 줄이려면 쉬운 과제부터 차근차근 연습해야 한다.
(2) 뛰어난 음악가는 연습 시간의 대부분을 어려운 부분에 쓴다.
(3) 연습의 양보다 실전 경험이 실력 향상에 더 중요하다.
(4) 학습자는 실수를 했을 때 감정을 잘 다스려야 한다.

sentences: [0] On a hot summer afternoon, the air above a parking lot can be several degrees warmer than the air in a nearby park.
[1] This difference is not simply a matter of shade.
[2] Trees also release water vapor through their leaves, and this process uses heat from the surrounding air.
[3] A single large tree can move hundreds of liters of water into the air on a sunny day.
[4] For this reason, planting trees is one of the most effective and least expensive ways for cities to cool themselves.
[5] Air conditioners, by contrast, cool the inside of buildings while pushing even more heat into the streets.
[6] A city that wants cooler summers should therefore think of its trees as part of its infrastructure, not as decoration.
stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: (0) 도시의 주차장은 공원보다 기온이 높다.
(1) 나무는 잎을 통해 많은 양의 물을 공기 중으로 내보낸다.
(2) 나무를 심는 것은 도시의 기온을 낮추는 효과적이고 저렴한 방법이다.
(3) 에어컨 사용을 줄이면 도시 전체의 에너지를 아낄 수 있다.
(4) 도시의 아름다움을 위해 나무를 장식으로 활용해야 한다.

sentences: [0] Many new employees hesitate to ask questions because they worry that colleagues will think they are incompetent.
[1] Studies of workplaces suggest that this worry is mostly unfounded.
[2] People who ask for advice are usually judged as more capable, not less, especially when the question is specific.
[3] Being asked for help also makes the person asked feel respected, which tends to improve the relationship.
[4] Newcomers, then, gain far more than they lose by asking thoughtful questions early.
[5] Waiting too long can be costly, since small misunderstandings grow into larger mistakes.
stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: (0) 신입 직원은 동료의 평가를 지나치게 의식한다.
(1) 구체적인 질문이 막연한 질문보다 답을 얻기 쉽다.
(2) 도움을 청하면 상대방과의 관계가 좋아진다.
(3) 신입 직원은 일찍 사려 깊은 질문을 하는 것이 훨씬 이롭다.
(4) 작은 오해는 시간이 지나면 저절로 풀린다.

sentences: [0] Parents often rush to fill every empty moment of a child's day with activities.
[1] The intention is good, but it may take away something valuable.
[2] Periods of boredom push children to invent their own games, stories, and projects.
[3] When nothing is provided, the mind starts to look for something to do, and that search is where creativity often begins.
[4] In one study, children who first copied numbers from a list for fifteen minutes later came up with more original uses for a paper cup.
[5] A certain amount of unplanned, even dull, time is therefore something children need rather than something to be avoided.
stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: (0) 아이들의 하루를 다양한 활동으로 채워 주어야 한다.
(1) 지루한 반복 작업은 아이들의 집중력을 높인다.
(2) 아이들에게는 계획되지 않은 지루한 시간이 어느 정도 필요하다.
(3) 창의성은 타고난 재능보다 노력으로 길러진다.
(4) 부모는 아이와 함께 놀이를 만들어야 한다.

sentences: [0] Relying on turn-by-turn directions may be weakening our ability to understand the places we live in.
[1] When a device tells us where to turn, we no longer need to build a mental picture of how streets connect.
[2] Drivers who navigate this way often cannot draw even a rough map of a route they have taken many times.
[3] Some people argue that this hardly matters, since the device is always available.
[4] But devices fail, batteries die, and signals disappear, and a person with no sense of direction is then truly lost.
[5] Moreover, the effort of finding our way seems to keep the brain's memory system active.
stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: (0) 길 안내 기기는 운전자의 안전을 높여 준다.
(1) 길 안내 기기에 의존하면 장소를 이해하는 능력이 약해질 수 있다.
(2) 배터리와 신호 문제 때문에 길 안내 기기는 믿을 수 없다.
(3) 기억력을 높이려면 지도를 직접 그려 보아야 한다.
(4) 기기는 늘 쓸 수 있으므로 방향 감각은 중요하지 않다.

sentences: [0] Shoppers tend to trust products labeled "natural" more than those without such a label.
[1] Many assume the word guarantees that the food is healthier or safer.
[2] In most countries, however, there is no legal definition of "natural" for food.
[3] A sugary drink full of additives can carry the label as easily as fresh fruit.
[4] The word, in short, tells buyers far less than they believe it does.
[5] Reading the list of ingredients is a much more reliable way to judge what is inside the package.
stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: (0) Why Natural Foods Taste Better
(1) The Empty Promise of the "Natural" Label
(2) How Additives Make Drinks Sweeter
(3) Laws That Protect Shoppers Everywhere
(4) Fresh Fruit: The Healthiest Choice

sentences: [0] Most students study in order to pass an exam.
[1] A different goal, however, may lead to deeper learning: preparing to explain the material to someone else.
[2] To teach, one must organize ideas into a clear order and find the links between them.
[3] Gaps in understanding become obvious when one tries to put an idea into simple words.
[4] In experiments, students told they would have to teach a passage remembered more of it than students told they would be tested, even though no one actually taught.
[5] The expectation of teaching, it seems, changes the way people study.
stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: (0) the stress students feel before exams
(1) the difficulty of explaining ideas in simple words
(2) the learning benefit of preparing to teach others
(3) the best way for teachers to design tests
(4) why studying alone is better than studying in groups

sentences: [0] It seems logical that working longer hours without stopping should get more done.
[1] Yet the mind does not work like a machine that runs at the same speed all day.
[2] Attention fades after a period of focused effort, and mistakes begin to increase.
[3] Short breaks allow that attention to recover, so the work that follows is faster and more accurate.
[4] Office workers who took a few minutes off every hour, for instance, finished tasks with fewer errors than those who worked straight through.
[5] Regular breaks are thus not a loss of working time but a way to make that time count.
stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: (0) 일을 잘하려면 쉬지 않고 오래 일해야 한다.
(1) 집중력은 하루 중 아침 시간에 가장 높다.
(2) 실수를 줄이려면 작업 결과를 꼼꼼히 검토해야 한다.
(3) 사무실 환경이 업무 성과를 좌우한다.
(4) 규칙적인 짧은 휴식은 일하는 시간을 더 가치 있게 만든다.

sentences: [0] Good writers, it is often assumed, produce excellent sentences on the first try.
[1] In reality, almost every strong piece of writing begins as a messy first draft.
[2] The first draft is where writers discover what they actually want to say.
[3] Only after the ideas are on the page can they be rearranged, cut, and sharpened.
[4] Professional editors report that most published articles have gone through several rounds of revision.
[5] Learning to write well, then, is largely learning to revise.
stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: (0) 훌륭한 작가는 첫 문장부터 완벽하게 쓴다.
(1) 글을 잘 쓰는 법을 배우는 것은 대부분 고쳐 쓰는 법을 배우는 것이다.
(2) 출판된 글은 여러 번 편집자의 손을 거친다.
(3) 초고에서는 문장보다 생각을 먼저 정리해야 한다.
(4) 글쓰기 능력은 많이 읽을수록 향상된다.
